messages.content: I want a "generate" section for the RL workspace that turns a natural-language prompt into Jac code. Give it a prompt textarea (pre-filled with an example like a simple add function) and a generate button. On click, call the backend to sample 8 completions from our SFT model and keep the first one that actually compiles and runs — the Jac compiler itself is the verifier. Because that call is blocking and can take a minute or two (it loads a 30B model per call), show a running elapsed-seconds counter while it works, gracefully handle a "busy" rejection from the server, and when it finishes display the returned Jac in a code block with a note saying whether it was verified. Make sure the timer gets cleaned up if the user leaves the section.

Shopping-list endpoints: generate_list(meal) clears old ShoppingItems, calls generate_shopping_list, persists each ingredient as a node (lowercased unit), returns list; plus get_shopping_list and clear_shopping_list.
Sandbox file ops: write_file, read_file (text and base64 binary), delete_file, and list_files.

Model the ESTree specification for JavaScript syntax trees as a set of typed data objects, for example a source-location record, a line/column position, and node types such as an identifier tagged with its literal type string, so an ECMAScript parser can build and consume them.

Implement the builder for the @jaseci/runtime npm package. Provide a helper for the runtime source path (runtimelib/client_runtime.cl.jac), a cached scan of that source for its public API names (top-level def/glob, optionally async or carrying an access tag), a cached compile of the runtime to a JavaScript string (raising if compilation errors), a function that intersects the JS top-level declarations with the API names to get the real export list, a package.json generator, and the tarball builder that compiles the JS, appends an export block, and packs package.json plus index.js, plus a variant that writes the .tgz to an output dir.
Fibonacci generator up to a limit, advancing via tuple swap.

Type-driven fake-data generator (non-LLM fallback). random_value_for_type(tp, depth cap) covering primitives, Optional/Union, Literal, Annotated, NewType, enums, TypedDict, namedtuple, dataclasses (recursive), datetimes, Decimal, and UUID; the internal type-probe helpers plus a returns_fake decorator.
Connect two Person nodes with a two-way relationship so the link runs in both directions.
_before_request hook walker holding the request dict; on Root entry, log its method and path.
Write a client-side component called Greeting that takes props and renders an h1 saying hello to the name passed in through those props.

Build a Calculator object in Jac that keeps a running value in memory, with methods to add to it, subtract from it, clear it, and read it back. Then add a natural-language method that takes a plain-English instruction and carries it out step by step by handing control to an LLM, giving the LLM those four memory methods as tools. Attach a short description of what that method does, and in the entry point run an instruction like 'start at 0, add 10, subtract 3, then add 5', printing both the result and the final memory value.
obj Student with name and a grades list, add_grade() and average() (0.0 on empty); add 90/85/92 and print the average.

Set up two page components for a Jac client app: a login page with a button that programmatically navigates to the dashboard, and a dashboard page that is protected — if the visitor is not logged in, redirect them to the login route instead of rendering.

Write a walker that traverses a graph of people breadth-first. Starting at the root it announces its position, then at each Person node it prints the name and queues that person's outgoing neighbors for later.
Route layout component: Navigation, a centered main hosting an Outlet, and a footer.

Write a walker that searches all Item nodes hanging off root for ones whose name contains a given query string (ignoring case), computes a relevance score for each hit, and returns the matches ordered from most to least relevant.

Create the publisher-pipeline package module for `jac bundle`: re-export the wheel builder plus the metadata helpers (the package-name normalizer and the metadata generator) and the wheel-filename helper, exposing them through __all__.

I need a walker that, at each Item it visits, inspects the graph around it -- all outgoing and incoming edges, only the connections made through a Link edge, and among those the ones whose weight exceeds 5. Set up the Item node and Link edge too.

I need a cross-backend equivalence test for a shared module-level declaration. Using the run_with_both harness, add a test that executes the shared_obj.jac fixture across all three targets -- the shared_py, shared_cl and shared_na entry points -- with the na and cl backends required, verifying that a type declared once and referenced (without redeclaration) by every backend yields the same result.

Write a private walker that deletes a todo and all of its children. Given a parent id, it should traverse from the root and delete any Todo node that either is the target or lists the target as its parent.

Put together two things in one program: a classic FizzBuzz function mapping a number to its Fizz/Buzz/FizzBuzz/number string, and a countdown generator; then print the FizzBuzz results for 1 through 15 and the countdown from 5.

Write a function that scans a block of text line by line, finds the first line that (after stripping whitespace) begins with the marker 'BENCH_JSON ', and JSON-decodes whatever follows the marker, returning the decoded value. If that line's payload isn't valid JSON, or no such line exists, return None. Test it against several strings covering a good object, an array, no marker, malformed JSON, and a bare number.
Boolean logic both ways: word forms (and/or/not) and their &&/|| symbol equivalents.
Backend+frontend skeleton: a Todo node, a get_todos walker iterating the todo children of root and reporting each, and an app() rendering a state string.

Write a simple App component that renders a heading and a plain button, and leave an inline note in the markup reminding us to swap that button out for a custom Button component later. The note should be a JSX comment, not a rendered element.
Write a minimal client app component that renders a Hello, World heading inside a div.

Build the message-thread renderer for our chat UI. User messages are right-aligned pills; assistant messages are left-aligned blocks. Split each assistant message into prose and fenced code segments: render the code segments as labelled, copy-able output panes (reuse our CodeBlock) and render the prose through react-markdown with GitHub-flavored markdown so headings, bold, lists, tables and links actually format, mapping each markdown element to our own design tokens rather than pulling in a typography plugin. When two assistant messages belong to the same compare group, show them side by side in a two-column grid of dashed panes labelled per model. Show a streaming caret while a message generates, an error box on failure, a stats footer (tokens per second, token count, times), and a SAVE EXAMPLE button that captures the user-to-assistant turn and briefly flips to SAVED.

I'm building the TRAIN section of the studio and it's a big one — write it as a client component with three subtabs: LAUNCH, MONITOR, and HISTORY. LAUNCH is a config form (base model HF id for SFT runs, a short name, an sft/dpo mode toggle, and the mode-specific option fields — eval-every/subset/dry-iters for SFT, dpo-iters/lr/beta for DPO) with start and stop buttons and a live RUN STATUS panel showing the job's status, pid, start time, last iteration, and a log tail; once a run is launched, the status panel and stop button must stay pinned to that specific run even as I keep editing the form. MONITOR lets me pick among currently running sessions as chips, shows a LIVE / STALLED / NO FEED indicator (calling it stalled when the iteration count stops advancing across several polls), and renders a live run detail — headline tiles (accuracy/test-pass, last iter, final loss, tokens/sec), two holdout idiomatic tiles, four charts (loss, learning rate, tokens/sec, accuracy), and a log — polled every couple of seconds. HISTORY offers two views: a "runs" view to pick a finished model and stage and inspect one run in that same detail layout, and a "compare" view that overlays every run of a stage in a comparison table (bolding the best metric per row) plus multi-line accuracy and loss charts. Do the polling with manual effects and intervals that re-arm whenever their dependencies change so you never read stale state, and back the whole thing with the train and runs server modules.

DATA section component (01 SFT/DPO workspace), two-column. Left: pipeline rail of the dataset build stages grouped (seed / idiom batches / scale / dpo / manifest+splits / holdouts / audit), per-stage status glyph + RUN (fires a detached builder job) + a done/total progress bar + a log tail for the selected stage; plus an add-examples panel (sft|dpo segmented, JSONL textarea, append, show added/total and any errors). Right: six stat tiles (sft total, dpo pairs, mlx sft split, mlx dpo split, function holdout, graph holdout) over a paginated read-only RowBrowser of the dataset files. Poll list_builders every 3s while active; clear the interval on exit/hide.

Build a graph of cities and roads (cities with a name and population, roads with a distance) and write a walker that walks it from the root, visiting each connected city, noting its name, and printing the city with its population.
Per-user data-fetch walker: gather the MyData children of root and report them.

I'm building the backend for a small social network in Jac — profiles, tweets, following, channels, the usual. I want it done the object-spatial way, where the data lives in a graph of Profile, Tweet, and Channel nodes and every operation is a walker that spawns at the caller's root and traverses out to do its work. Could you write the walkers for it? Setting up and retrieving a profile, posting and deleting tweets, liking and commenting, building a personalized feed from my own plus followed users' tweets (with optional keyword search), surfacing trending hashtags across everyone, and the channel side — creating, joining, leaving, and posting to channels.

I need the membership step of a join-channel walker in Jac. On the target channel, look up the acting user's profile and, only if there's no membership edge yet, connect the profile to the channel with a Member edge; joining again should be a no-op. Then report success and stop.

I want to see how walkers traverse a graph in Jac. Create some Item nodes under root, then write a walker that carries a target name, walks the outgoing nodes, gathers every item whose name equals the target into a list and emits them as reports — and have the node print a greeting whenever the walker arrives.
Create a Road edge that knows its distance, and whenever a Traveler walker crosses it, add that distance onto the traveler's running total.

CaptureRunner.record(name, status, detail): append {step, status, detail} to self.results; derive a 4-char mark ('ok  '/'skip'/'FAIL' by status, else-FAIL default); print `  [<mark>] <name>: <detail>`.

Spec: get_guestbook walker, on Root exit. Sort self.results in place by created_at in descending order using a lambda whose parameter is typed as GuestEntry, then report the first 50 entries. GuestEntry carries id/name/message/created_at.
Create a few Person nodes and wire up a small graph — connect a couple of them to root, and connect one person to another.
Nested error boundaries: an app-level boundary wrapping header/content/footer, plus an inner boundary scoped to the main content, each with a distinct fallback.
_log(msg: str) -> None: print msg with a '>> ' prefix.

We have a semantic-annotation system where a developer can declare a symbol in one file and give its semantic string definition in another; write the pass that matches them up. As a Transform over the module, connect each SemDef to the declaration it annotates, resolving dotted names for nested symbols, and warn about any semantic definition that fails to match a declaration. Expose the transform entry point, a resolver that finds the target symbol for a SemDef given a scope, and a routine that links the semantic definitions from a source symbol table into a target symbol table.
Two globals (typed float PI, empty dict config); entry block prints PI.

Define a Person object with a name and age, and add a post-initialization hook that prints a 'Created ...' message right after the object is built. Give it a greet method as well, then construct one and greet.

Build the in-memory topology index that stores a compact adjacency structure on root nodes so type-filtered edge chains can be resolved without loading every node from the database. Keep a canonical adjacency list of (source, edge-type, target) triples alongside a type-keyed bucket map with MRO fan-out, and provide methods to add and remove nodes and edges, resolve a hop chain to a candidate UUID set (bailing when an intermediate hop crosses into a foreign root), resolve a single ordered hop with a slice, look up cross-root ids, and encode/decode itself to a versioned binary format.
Broadcasting async WebSocket walker ChatRoom: fan out each {sender, content} message to all connections; sender defaults to anonymous.

Write the ambient builtins module that the Jac runtime exposes to user code. It should declare the APIProtocol and ScheduleTrigger string enums, a set of private lazy accessor functions that fetch runtime pieces on demand (the Jac interface, access levels, jid/jobj, grant/revoke, allroots, save/commit/store, the LLM model, the archetype alias), a module-level `__getattr__` for lazy attribute resolution, and public helpers like printgraph, restspec, schedule, a portable `new()` constructor, and an `unsafe_html` marker for raw HTML — then publish the public surface through `__all__`.

I need a utility class that copies static asset files — stylesheets, images, fonts, audio and video — from one directory into another. It should hold the set of recognized asset file extensions and offer methods to copy general assets, TypeScript files, and any custom asset types, with an option to preserve the source folder structure.
Create a search component that re-runs an async search whenever the typed query changes and lists the returned results, keeping both the query and results in state.

Internal (non-:pub) log/metric parsers for Train/Evals. parse_train_log(path) -> {train,val,lr,tps:[{x,y}], last_iter} across SFT+DPO formats; read_series(path,ykey) -> [{x:step,y}] skipping non-object rows; last_row(path); tail(path,n=40); last_iter(path) via regex; merge_by_x(by_run) -> x-keyed overlay rows sorted by x; stages(run_dir) from .<stage>.done markers; idiom_summary(run_dir,mode,kind) last-row picker preferring function over graph and requiring avg_sim. Keep regex/json results in any locals; int/float via int(str())/float(str()).
Task node (title, done=False); entry block wires three Task instances off root with `++>` and prints a done message.

Using plain objects, model people who each keep a list of friends, with a method that links two people as mutual friends; build a small friend network and then print out one person's friends, the manual non-graph way.
Coordinator walker: on Root entry, spawn Researcher(topic), Writer(style), Reviewer off root, then report a dict of their .reports (research/draft/review).

I'm building the projection math for a 3D renderer. Write a function that, given the six clip-plane values (left, right, bottom, top, near, far), returns a perspective frustum matrix as a flat list of 16 floats in column-major order, with the standard OpenGL glFrustum entries in their slots and zeros everywhere else.

Show how to modify a module-level global variable from inside a Jac function. Declare a global integer counter and write a function that increments it, using the `global` declaration so the assignment affects the outer variable.

Write a Jac walker example that demonstrates control flow inside a handler -- that reporting a value and then visiting connected nodes both proceed normally, while a return statement would stop the walker. Comment each line to explain what continues and what halts.

In-memory graph topology index for query optimization. Dual structures — canonical adjacency triples plus type-keyed buckets with MRO fan-out. Methods: add/remove nodes and edges, resolve a typed hop chain to a candidate UUID set (bailing on cross-root intermediates), ordered single-hop slice resolution, cross-root id lookup, and binary encode/decode (format v2).
Illustrate LEGB shadowing: same identifier bound at global, enclosing-function, and inner-function scope; show which binding each print resolves to.

I want to demonstrate how a depth-first traversal behaves on different graph topologies. Write a tracer walker that appends each node's value and then visits its successors, plus a guarded variant that skips nodes it has already recorded. Run the plain tracer over a straight chain, a diamond (whose shared sink gets visited twice because the kernel doesn't track visited nodes automatically), and a fan-out, and run the guarded tracer over a cycle so it stops instead of looping forever. Collect the four seen-lists into one result, with a Python driver and a client-codespace equivalent.

Build a file-based route scanner that turns a pages/ directory into a route tree following a Next.js-style convention. Define a RouteEntry record (url path, component import, file path, auth flag, layout and catch-all flags, nested children) and a RouteScanner that walks the pages directory, recognizes layout and index files and an auth route group, maps filenames to route paths and component names, and detects route collisions.
Exercise all arithmetic ops including % and ** plus parenthesized precedence; print 8, 42, 16.

```jac
with entry {
    # Basic math
    sum = 5 + 3;        # Addition: 8
    difference = 10 - 4; # Subtraction: 6
    product = 6 * 7;     # Multiplication: 42
    quotient = 20 / 4;   # Division: 5.0

    print(sum);         # Shows: 8
    print(product);     # Shows: 42

    # More operations
    remainder = 17 % 5;  # Modulo (remainder): 2
    power = 2 ** 3;      # Exponent: 8 (2³)

    # Combined operations
    total = (5 + 3) * 2;  # Use parentheses like in math: 16

    print(total);
}
```

Implement the annex-loading pass. Its transform should skip stub-only modules, non-.jac modules, and modules already annexable by another, and otherwise load and attach annexes to the module. The loading helper should discover the module's .impl.jac and .test.jac annex files and its variant files, compile each without codegen, and append the resulting modules to the node's impl, test, and variant lists respectively.
Operation-plus-result walker: create Item(name) off root and report the created node, typed for hydration on the client side.

Explain the difference between the two kinds of entry blocks in Jac with an example: a default entry that always runs when the module loads, and a __main__ entry that only runs when the file is executed directly.

Walker PrioritizeTickets in Jac: from Root, visit [-->], and per Ticket entry assign here.priority from an `analyze_priority(title, description) -> Priority by llm()`, report, then visit [-->] onward. Define the Priority enum (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) and Ticket{title, description, priority=MEDIUM}.
Walker that reports here.age at each Person and continues traversing; collect the results from the spawn return value. Use a three-node chain.

In a little 3D shooter I keep a fixed-size pool of bullet objects and reuse dead ones. Write a fire routine that shoots a bullet along the current aim. Convert the global yaw and pitch (degrees) to radians using DEG2RAD, then build the aim direction from them: dx = -sin(yaw)*cos(pitch), dy = sin(pitch), dz = -cos(yaw)*cos(pitch), using the provided jcos/jsin helpers. Scan the bullet list from the front, and for the first bullet whose life is 0 or less, place it at the player position (px, py, pz), set its velocity to the aim direction times a speed of 40, set its life to 2.0, and stop.

yaw_basis: given yaw_r (radians), derive XZ forward/right basis — fwd_x=-jsin(yaw_r), fwd_z=-jcos(yaw_r), rgt_x=jcos(yaw_r), rgt_z=-jsin(yaw_r); return [fwd_x, fwd_z, rgt_x, rgt_z]. Use provided jsin/jcos. Driver over a yaw list printing round(v,6).
Jac `divide(a, b)` that raises ValueError on a zero divisor; call it inside try/except ValueError/finally printing the error and 'Done'.
Numeric literals: decimal/hex/octal/binary ints, a float, scientific notation, and underscore digit separators.
One-file app: a User node, a get_user walker (Root entry, empty report), and an app() component.

LLM sales agent in Jac over global products/prices/inventory dicts. Tools: list_products, get_price, check_inventory (in-stock/out/not-found), and place_order (validates existence and stock, then decrements). `sales_agent(request) -> str by llm(tools=[...])` with sem 'Browse products, check prices and availability, and place orders.' Entry: three customer turns -- catalog, price+stock, and an order.

I'd like a Jac generator for a third round of conversion examples -- this one should push into the trickier idioms: typed-edge filters, walkers that visit more than one node type, enum-based state machines, and static methods. Store each as a Python/Jac pair with a difficulty and expected output, append them to the conversion dataset, then re-validate every appended example by running it and print how many held up.
Comment(c): render the author heading plus the trusted HTML injected raw via unsafe_html().
Client import block: react hooks (useState/useEffect/useCallback), @tanstack/react-query (useQuery, useMutation), lodash (debounce, throttle), axios default.
Write an object type Foo with an integer field, and give it a constructor that takes an int, calls the parent initializer, and stores the value into the field.

Define a few edge types: a Friend edge that records the year it started and a strength defaulting to 1.0, a plain Follows edge with no data, and a Weighted edge that holds a weight and exposes a method returning that weight normalized against a supplied maximum.

Create a small analytics function that produces an AnalyticsReport from a signature count: set its pid to the current process id, set its score to the count converted to float and multiplied by 1.5, and leave the service name at its default of 'analytics'.
setup_profile run on Root entry: visit [-->[?:Profile]]; in the else branch (nothing enqueued) create a Profile on root with created_at = "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z", grant ConnectPerm, and visit it.

ReadWriteLock over a threading.Condition: concurrent readers, exclusive writer, writer-priority (readers block while writers_waiting > 0), non-reentrant. Implement acquire_read/release_read, acquire_write/release_write, and @contextmanager read_lock/write_lock (release in finally).

obj UniPass(ModuleCodegenPass): has term_signal/prune_signal; declared postinit, before_pass, after_pass, enter_node, exit_node, prune, recalculate_parents, transform(Module)->Module, traverse. Implement the static get_all_sub_nodes(nd, typ, brute_force=False) (sub_node_tab lookup, else recursive kid walk under brute_force, else raise), find_parent_of_type(nd, typ), and has_parent_of_node(nd, parent).

I need a single re-export point for Jac's core runtime constructs. Gather the archetype types, including the walker archetype and walker anchor along with the node and edge equivalents, the Root node, the generic edge, the access-level helpers, and the object-spatial function type, together with the MTIR/MTRuntime symbols, and re-export everything under an explicit __all__.

```jac
"""Core constructs for Jac Language - re-exports."""
import from jaclang.jac0core.archetype {
    AccessLevel,
    access_level_cast,
    Anchor,
    Archetype,
    EdgeAnchor,
    EdgeArchetype,
    GenericEdge,
    JsxElement,
    NodeAnchor,
    NodeArchetype,
    ObjectSpatialFunction,
    PermissionDenied,
    Root,
    WalkerAnchor,
    WalkerArchetype
}
import from jaclang.jac0core.mtp { MTIR, MTRuntime }
glob __all__ = [
         'AccessLevel',
         'access_level_cast',
         'Anchor',
         'NodeAnchor',
         'EdgeAnchor',
         'WalkerAnchor',
         'Archetype',
         'NodeArchetype',
         'EdgeArchetype',
         'WalkerArchetype',
         'GenericEdge',
         'JsxElement',
         'PermissionDenied',
         'Root',
         'MTIR',
         'MTRuntime',
         'ObjectSpatialFunction'
     ];

```

Illustrate how node exit abilities fire in reverse order after a depth-first descent. Define a Step node with a label and a Logger walker that prints 'ENTER: <label>' on the way in and 'EXIT: <label>' on the way out, so that along a root->A->B->C chain the exits print C, then B, then A.

Model customers, products, and a Purchased edge holding a rating, then write a walker that takes a customer, gathers their top-rated buys, walks to people who bought the same items and liked them, and suggests those buyers' other favorites minus what the customer already has. Build sample purchase data and print suggestions for one customer.
Write a small badge primitive in Jac — a status pill that shows a label, optionally takes a style variant, and optionally renders a little pulsing dot before the label to signal live activity.
obj with has fields: required str, int = 0, list[str] = [], dict[str,int] = {}.

HttpStatus enum (OK=200, NOT_FOUND=404) with an inline-Python is_success() method and a message @property.

Show the different ways to launch a walker. Define an Item node with a value and a walker that reports each item's value as it traverses; build a three-node chain under root, then spawn the walker both with default parameters and with a parameter supplied, and print the collected reports.

I want a benchmark driver in Jac for our OSP region experiments — the osp_regions kernels — that covers four of them. For reg_graph, run a build-traverse-discard benchmark across region vs bare, rc vs cycles, and acyclic vs cyclic configurations, checking that every cell of a given config yields an identical output digest and reporting medians alongside tail-latency and drop-count metrics; produce the 'bare' variant by feeding the source through our rerase.jac transform. For reg_wspawn, measure walker-spawn reclamation under rc and cycles. For reg_transfer, compare move vs copy vs serial strategies across a range of subgraph sizes, confirm digest identity across strategies at each size, and report per-transfer nanoseconds. For reg_overhead, micro-benchmark region_of allocation, managed vs region-anchored. Each measurement should compile the kernel with `jac nacompile` under the right GC mode, run it N times under /usr/bin/time -v, parse the kernel's ns= and 'm:'-prefixed metric lines and treat the remaining stdout as the identity digest. Give it --invocations, --quick and --out flags, fail loudly on any digest mismatch, and write everything to JSON.
find_profile run on Root entry: if self.target_id is set, target = jobj(self.target_id); visit [target] only when it is an instance of Profile.
Define three typed functions: an int add(a, b); a str greet(name) returning a formatted 'Hello, name!'; and a void log(message) that prints it prefixed with [LOG].
PyBytecodeGenPass(Transform[Module,Module]) declaration: transform(ir_in) -> Module, process_modules(root_module), compile_module_to_bytecode(mod). Docstrings and signatures only.

In my Jac social graph, implement the tweet-deletion step of a walker. It fires when the walker lands on a Tweet, and only when both the tweet id and the author match what the request specifies; then it removes that tweet from the graph, returns a success result, and disengages.
join_channel: act on the target channel, create a Member edge from the caller's profile to here only if none exists (idempotent), report {'success': True}, disengage.
Iterate a list of fruits two ways, directly over the items and by index, printing each element.

Show me how to consume those results clearly: instead of relying on bare magic indices, document what each report position means and read them defensively with sensible defaults when a position might be missing.
Chainable QueryBuilder: from_table(t) and limit(n) mutate state and return Self for fluent chaining; show a chained construction.

Replace our SQLite chat storage with Jac's graph persistence. Model chats and their messages as nodes hanging off the shared root (root --> Chat --> Msg) so they survive restarts, each addressable by a stable id. Give me plain view objects for chats and messages, node types with a to-view method, and endpoints to list a workspace's chats most-recently-updated first (treating chats with no workspace field as workspace '01'), create a chat, rename one, delete a chat along with all its messages, fetch a chat's messages, and append a message while bumping the chat's updated timestamp. Timestamps in UTC, plus a helper returning today's UTC date for the sidebar's day grouping.

Module surface for enum type-checking in the Jac type checker: define the reserved-enum-member-names set, plus stubbed signatures for excluding reserved member names, building EnumMemberInfo from an assignment statement, validating a member's explicit annotation against its value type, assembling the enum-members map for an enum or class-based enum, and resolving a special enum subclass's value type from its base classes.

RL ladder results backend. _pivot(path): parse ladder JSONL rows tagged r<N>/<model>/<cond>/<gen|mem>, last-write-wins per (model,rung,cond), return {cells, curve (rung-indexed, one line per model-cond gen pass@1, densified with None), curve_keys, families, count}. get_rl_ladder() -> primary + sg + v84 runs. get_rl_corrected() merges corrected_summary.json over an empty shape carrying every client-dereferenced key. rl_generate(prompt,k=8): heavy_acquire the lock, subprocess the best-of-k generator, return {ok,verified,jac,note,k}. External JSON, so the pivot stays Any-typed (parse-gated, not strict-checked).
Two endpoints: a public get_status() returning an ok status, and a private get_user_data() that is per-user isolated.
Write just the declaration of a CircleService object: a name field and a describe method whose implementation is provided separately.
I need a walker that traverses a graph reporting each node's value as it goes: on entering a node it should report the node's value field, then move on to whatever that node connects to.
Profile-entry gather: append here.to_user_view() to self.results.

```jac
"""Icon set — NATIVE variant (Lucide via `lucide-react-native`, real RN SVG).

The compiler picks this file over `icon.cl.jac` for the react-native target.
`lucide-react-native` peer-depends on `react-native-svg`, which Metro bundles
correctly on native (the incompatibility is only with the web/Vite pipeline —
which never sees this file, since web uses `icon.cl.jac`). Same `<Icon/>` API.
"""

cl {
    import from "lucide-react-native" {
        House,
        Search,
        Bell,
        User,
        Heart,
        MessageCircle,
        Repeat2,
        SquarePen,
        LogOut,
        Lock,
        AtSign,
        Star,
        Calendar,
        X,
        Send,
        Image as ImageIcon
    }

    # name → Lucide component. Same keys exist in icon.cl.jac.
    glob LUCIDE = {
             home: House,
             search: Search,
             bell: Bell,
             user: User,
             heart: Heart,
             comment: MessageCircle,
             repeat: Repeat2,
             edit: SquarePen,
             logout: LogOut,
             lock: Lock,
             at: AtSign,
             spark: Star,
             calendar: Calendar,
             close: X,
             send: Send,
             image: ImageIcon
         };

    """Render a Lucide icon by name. `fill` paints it solid in its own color
    (active like / brand mark); `width` is the stroke weight."""
    def:pub Icon(
        name: str, size: int, color: str, fill: bool, width: float
    ) -> JsxElement {
        Glyph = LUCIDE[name];
        return
            <Glyph
                size={size}
                color={color}
                fill={(color if fill else "none")}
                strokeWidth={width}
            />;
    }
}
```

Define the `jac eject` command, which converts a Jac project into standalone Python and JavaScript with no .jac files left. Give it a positional source directory defaulting to the current one, an --output option for the destination, and a --force flag to overwrite an existing output, plus usage examples, filed under the project group.

```jac
"""Eject command: convert a Jac project to standalone Python + JavaScript.

Walks a Jac project, compiles every .jac source file to its Python and
JavaScript equivalents, copies static assets, and writes a runnable project
folder containing zero .jac files. The ejected backend still imports from
the installed `jaclang` runtime library at execution time, but no Jac source
or compilation step is required to run it.
"""

import from jaclang.cli.command { Arg, ArgKind }
import from jaclang.cli.registry { get_registry }

glob registry = get_registry();

"""Eject a Jac project to standalone Python + JavaScript."""
@registry.command(
    name="eject",
    help="Eject a Jac project to standalone Python + JavaScript",
    args=[
        Arg.create(
            "source",
            kind=ArgKind.POSITIONAL,
            default=".",
            help="Project directory to eject (default: current directory)"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "output",
            default="",
            help="Output directory (default: <name>-ejected next to source)",
            short="o"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "force",
            typ=bool,
            default=False,
            help="Overwrite output directory if it already exists",
            short="f"
        ),

    ],
    examples=[
        ("jac eject", "Eject the current project to ./<name>-ejected/"),
        ("jac eject . -o /tmp/myapp", "Eject current project to /tmp/myapp"),
        ("jac eject myapp --force", "Eject myapp/, overwriting existing output"),

    ],
    group="project"
)
def eject(source: str = ".", output: str = "", force: bool = False) -> int;

```

```jac
"""Semantic Token Manager module."""
import from typing { List, Optional, Tuple }
import logging;

import jaclang.jac0core.unitree as uni;
import from jaclang { JacRuntimeInterface as Jac }
import from jaclang.langserve.utils {
    find_surrounding_tokens,
    get_token_start,
    get_line_of_code
}
import jaclang.lsp.types as lspt;

# Semantic token flat array field offsets.
# Each token occupies TOK_STRIDE (5) consecutive ints:
#   [line_delta, col_delta, length, token_type, token_modifier]
glob TOK_LINE_DELTA = 0,
     TOK_COL_DELTA = 1,
     TOK_LENGTH = 2,
     TOK_TYPE = 3,
     TOK_MODIFIER = 4,
     TOK_STRIDE = 5,
     logger = logging.getLogger("jaclang.langserve.sem_manager");

"""Semantic Token Manager class."""
obj SemTokManager {
    has ir: uni.Module,
        hub: dict = {},
        sem_tokens: List[int] by postinit,
        static_sem_tokens:
            List[Tuple[(lspt.Position, int, int, uni.AstSymbolNode)]] by postinit;

    def postinit -> None;
    def collect_resolved_nodes(ir: uni.Module) -> list;
    def gen_sem_tokens(ir: uni.Module) -> list[int];
    def gen_sem_tok_node(
        ir: uni.Module
    ) -> List[Tuple[(lspt.Position, int, int, uni.AstSymbolNode)]];

    def update_sem_tokens(
        content_changes: lspt.DidChangeTextDocumentParams,
        sem_tokens: list[int],
        document_lines: List[str]
    ) -> list[int];

    static def handle_multi_line_delete(
        self: SemTokManager,
        sem_tokens: list[int],
        next_token_index: int,
        nxt_tok_pos: tuple[(int, int, int)],
        change_start_line: int,
        change_end_line: int,
        change_start_char: int,
        change_end_char: int,
        prev_tok_pos: tuple[(int, int, int)],
        is_next_token_same_line: bool
    ) -> list[int];

    static def handle_single_line_delete_between_tokens(
        self: SemTokManager,
        sem_tokens: list[int],
        next_token_index: int,
        is_next_token_same_line: bool,
        change: lspt.TextDocumentContentChangeEvent_Type1,
        change_start_line: int,
        change_end_line: int
    ) -> list[int];

    static def handle_single_line_delete(
        self: SemTokManager,
        sem_tokens: list[int],
        next_token_index: int,
        prev_token_index: int,
        is_next_token_same_line: bool,
        change: lspt.TextDocumentContentChangeEvent_Type1
    ) -> list[int];

    static def handle_single_line_insertion(
        self: SemTokManager,
        sem_tokens: list[int],
        next_token_index: int,
        is_next_token_same_line: bool,
        change: lspt.TextDocumentContentChangeEvent_Type1,
        tokens_on_same_line: bool,
        nxt_tok_pos: tuple[(int, int, int)],
        change_start_line: int,
        line_delta: int
    ) -> list[int];

    static def handle_multi_line_insertion(
        self: SemTokManager,
        sem_tokens: list[int],
        next_token_index: int,
        nxt_tok_pos: tuple[(int, int, int)],
        change_start_line: int,
        change_end_line: int,
        change_end_char: int,
        prev_tok_pos: tuple[(int, int, int)],
        tokens_on_same_line: bool,
        changing_line_text: tuple[(str, int)],
        line_delta: int
    ) -> list[int];

    static def handle_insert_inside_token(
        self: SemTokManager,
        change: lspt.TextDocumentContentChangeEvent_Type1,
        sem_tokens: list[int],
        prev_token_index: int,
        changing_line_text: tuple[(str, int)],
        line_delta: int,
        prev_tok_pos: tuple[(int, int, int)],
        change_start_char: int,
        change_end_char: int,
        is_token_boundary_edit: bool,
        nxt_tok_pos: tuple[(int, int, int)]
    ) -> tuple[list[int], bool, tuple[(int, int, int)], Optional[int]];
}
```

Write the maintenance hooks that keep each root's topology index in sync with graph mutations — all no-ops when the topology-index flag is off. Provide an enabled check (an env var overriding the toml flag), helpers to find a node's owning root, to get an archetype's type name and its user-defined MRO chain, and to index and unindex an edge into a given root, plus the event callbacks on_edge_created, on_edge_destroyed, on_node_saved, and on_node_destroyed.

```jac
"""Topology index maintenance hooks.

These functions keep root topology indices in sync with graph mutations
(edge create/destroy, node save/destroy). All are no-ops when the
topology_index config flag is disabled.

Query planning lives in `jaclang.runtimelib.planner` — this module only
mutates the index in response to runtime events. The cleanup boundary is
explicit: anything that *reads* the index for a query goes through the
planner; anything that *writes* the index in response to a graph mutation
stays here.
"""

import from uuid { UUID }

"""Check if topology_index is enabled. The `JAC_TOPOLOGY_INDEX` env var
overrides the toml flag (truthy: 1 / true / yes / on)."""
def _is_enabled -> bool;

"""Get the root NodeAnchor that owns this anchor."""
def _get_root_anchor(anchor: any) -> any;

"""Get the archetype class name."""
def _type_name(`obj: object) -> str;

"""Get the user-defined MRO chain for a node/edge archetype, stopping at the
runtime base archetypes (Node/Edge/Walker/Archetype/object). Concrete type
appears at index 0."""
def _get_type_mro(`obj: object) -> list[str];

"""Record an edge in the given root's topology index. Used by
`on_edge_created` to mirror cross-root edges into the indexes of both
endpoint owners (otherwise reverse queries from the target side would
miss the edge entirely)."""
def _index_edge_into(root_anchor: any, source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Remove an edge from the given root's topology index. Mirror of
`_index_edge_into` used by `on_edge_destroyed`."""
def _unindex_edge_from(root_anchor: any, source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Called after an edge is created between source and target."""
def on_edge_created(source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Called when an edge is destroyed."""
def on_edge_destroyed(source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Called when a node is saved/persisted. Ensures it's in the root's index."""
def on_node_saved(node_anchor: any) -> None;

"""Called when a node is destroyed."""
def on_node_destroyed(node_anchor: any) -> None;

```

Demonstrate f-string field alignment and padding in Jac -- setting a width, right/left/center alignment, and using a custom fill character.

```jac
def example() {
    name = "Alice";
    # Width specification
    f"{name:10}";           # "Alice     " (10 chars, left-aligned)
    f"{name:>10}";          # "     Alice" (right-aligned)
    f"{name:^10}";          # "  Alice   " (centered)
    f"{name:<10}";          # "Alice     " (left-aligned, explicit)

    # Fill character
    f"{name:*>10}";         # "*****Alice" (fill with *)
    f"{name:-^10}";         # "--Alice---" (centered with -)
}
```

Give me the native counterpart of my Lucide icon component for the React Native target, using lucide-react-native (which pulls in react-native-svg through Metro). Keep exactly the same <Icon name=.../> interface as the web version — the same set of named glyphs mapped to Lucide components, and an Icon function taking name, size, color, fill, and stroke width, painting the glyph solid in its own color when fill is true and outlined otherwise — so the compiler picks this file on native and the web file on web without any call site changing.

```jac
"""Icon set — NATIVE variant (Lucide via `lucide-react-native`, real RN SVG).

The compiler picks this file over `icon.cl.jac` for the react-native target.
`lucide-react-native` peer-depends on `react-native-svg`, which Metro bundles
correctly on native (the incompatibility is only with the web/Vite pipeline —
which never sees this file, since web uses `icon.cl.jac`). Same `<Icon/>` API.
"""

cl {
    import from "lucide-react-native" {
        House,
        Search,
        Bell,
        User,
        Heart,
        MessageCircle,
        Repeat2,
        SquarePen,
        LogOut,
        Lock,
        AtSign,
        Star,
        Calendar,
        X,
        Send,
        Image as ImageIcon
    }

    # name → Lucide component. Same keys exist in icon.cl.jac.
    glob LUCIDE = {
             home: House,
             search: Search,
             bell: Bell,
             user: User,
             heart: Heart,
             comment: MessageCircle,
             repeat: Repeat2,
             edit: SquarePen,
             logout: LogOut,
             lock: Lock,
             at: AtSign,
             spark: Star,
             calendar: Calendar,
             close: X,
             send: Send,
             image: ImageIcon
         };

    """Render a Lucide icon by name. `fill` paints it solid in its own color
    (active like / brand mark); `width` is the stroke weight."""
    def:pub Icon(
        name: str, size: int, color: str, fill: bool, width: float
    ) -> JsxElement {
        Glyph = LUCIDE[name];
        return
            <Glyph
                size={size}
                color={color}
                fill={(color if fill else "none")}
                strokeWidth={width}
            />;
    }
}

```

Scoped-style annex subsystem for the cl target: a .style.css sharing a base name with a .cl.jac module forms one auto-scoped unit. Provide ScopedStyleSheet(obj) holding module_path, css_path, source_css, class_map, scoped_css, with a postinit that parses the source and a rewrite_class_value() that hashes declared tokens and preserves others; hash_class_name(module_path, class) -> '<name>-<8 hex blake2s>'; scope_selector() rewriting a selector prelude, recording declared classes and unwrapping :global(...); scope_stylesheet() walking rules with brace tracking, scoping style-rule preludes, descending @media/@supports/@container/@layer/@scope, copying other at-rules and declaration blocks verbatim; load_style_annex() returning the scoped sheet or None; plus _skip_string, _consume_braced_block, and _grouping_at_rule helpers. Export the public names via __all__.

```jac
"""Scoped-style annex support for the `cl` (client) target.

A `.style.css` file that shares a base name with a `.cl.jac` module
(e.g. `card.style.css` alongside `card.cl.jac`) forms one logical module
with auto-scoped CSS classes. The compiler:

  1. Hashes every class selector declared in the annex with a per-module
     digest (`blake2s(module_path + class_name)`, truncated to 8 hex
     chars), producing names like `card-1a2b3c4d`.
  2. Rewrites the annex CSS so each declared selector uses the hashed
     form, leaving `:global(...)` selectors verbatim (the wrapper is
     stripped, the inner selector preserved).
  3. Exposes the hashed names so the ECMAScript pass can rewrite JSX
     `className`/`class` literals in the module that reference a declared
     class to the same hashed form.

The rewritten CSS is emitted as a sidecar artifact (`Module.gen.css`) and
a side-effect `import "./<base>.css";` is injected into the compiled JS so
the styles load with the component -- framework-neutral, no bundler config.

This subsystem is self-contained: annex discovery + CSS parse + selector
hashing all live here; the ECMAScript pass only consumes the resulting
`class_map` and `scoped_css`.
"""

import from hashlib { blake2s }
import from jaclang.jac0core.bccache { discover_style_annex }

"""A loaded, scoped `.style.css` annex for one client module.

    Construct via `load_style_annex`; `postinit` parses `source_css`,
    populating `class_map` (bare name -> hashed name) and `scoped_css`
    (the selector-rewritten stylesheet).
    """
obj ScopedStyleSheet {
    has module_path: str,
        css_path: str,
        source_css: str,
        class_map: dict[str, str] = {},
        scoped_css: str = '';

    def postinit -> None;
    """Rewrite a JSX `className`/`class` value, hashing each declared token.

        The value is split on whitespace; tokens that name a class declared
        in the annex are replaced with their hashed form, others are kept
        verbatim. Original inter-token spacing is collapsed to single
        spaces (semantically irrelevant for a class list).
        """
    def rewrite_class_value(value: str) -> str;
}

"""Hash a single class name with the module-scoped digest.

    Returns the scoped name `<class_name>-<8 hex>`. Deterministic for a
    given (module_path, class_name) pair, so the CSS selector rewrite and
    the JSX `className` rewrite agree.
    """
def hash_class_name(module_path: str, class_name: str) -> str;

"""Rewrite a CSS selector prelude, hashing declared class tokens.

    Class tokens (`.name`) are replaced with `.name-<hash>` and recorded in
    `class_map`; `:global(...)` regions are unwrapped and preserved
    verbatim; comments, strings, and attribute selectors are passed through
    untouched.
    """
def scope_selector(selector: str, module_path: str, class_map: dict[str, str]) -> str;

"""Rewrite a full stylesheet, scoping the class selectors of style rules.

    Walks rules with brace tracking: style-rule preludes are scoped via
    `scope_selector`; grouping at-rules (`@media`, `@supports`,
    `@container`, `@layer`, `@scope`) are descended into; other at-rules
    (`@keyframes`, `@font-face`, ...) and all declaration blocks are copied
    verbatim. Mutates `class_map` in place and returns the rewritten CSS.
    """
def scope_stylesheet(css: str, module_path: str, class_map: dict[str, str]) -> str;

"""Load and scope the `.style.css` annex for a module, or None if absent.

    `module_path` is the head module's source path (variant suffix is
    handled by `discover_style_annex`).
    """
def load_style_annex(module_path: str) -> (ScopedStyleSheet | None);
```

f-string numeric format specs: integer bases with zero-pad, float :.2f / :e / :g, :% percentage, and :, plus :_ grouping.

```jac
def example() {
    n = 42;
    pi = 3.14159265;

    # Integer formats
    f"{n:d}";               # "42" (decimal)
    f"{n:b}";               # "101010" (binary)
    f"{n:o}";               # "52" (octal)
    f"{n:x}";               # "2a" (hex lowercase)
    f"{n:X}";               # "2A" (hex uppercase)
    f"{n:05d}";             # "00042" (zero-padded, width 5)

    # Float formats
    f"{pi:f}";              # "3.141593" (fixed-point, 6 decimals default)
    f"{pi:.2f}";            # "3.14" (2 decimal places)
    f"{pi:10.2f}";          # "      3.14" (width 10, 2 decimals)
    f"{pi:e}";              # "3.141593e+00" (scientific notation)
    f"{pi:.2e}";            # "3.14e+00" (scientific, 2 decimals)
    f"{pi:g}";              # "3.14159" (general format)

    # Percentage
    ratio = 0.756;
    f"{ratio:.1%}";         # "75.6%"

    # Thousands separator
    big = 1234567;
    f"{big:,}";             # "1,234,567"
    f"{big:_}";             # "1_234_567" (underscore separator)
}
```

Execution-group command specs: `run` (filename plus main/cache/autonative/diagnostics/args), `enter` (filename/entrypoint/args plus root/node), `start` (REST server: port/main/faux/dev/api_port/no_client), and `debug` — all carrying examples.

```jac
"""Execution commands: run, enter, serve, debug.

Commands for running and debugging Jac programs.
"""

import from jaclang.cli.command { Arg, ArgKind }
import from jaclang.cli.registry { get_registry }

glob registry = get_registry();

"""Run the specified .jac or .py file."""
@registry.command(
    name="run",
    help="Run a Jac program",
    args=[
        Arg.create(
            "filename", kind=ArgKind.POSITIONAL, help="Path to .jac or .py file"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "main", typ=bool, default=True, help="Treat module as __main__", short="m"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "cache", typ=bool, default=True, help="Enable compilation cache", short="c"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "autonative",
            typ=bool,
            default=False,
            help="Auto-promote compatible modules to native execution (experimental)",
            short="N"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "profile",
            default="",
            short="",
            help="Configuration profile to load (e.g. prod, staging)"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "diagnostics",
            default="",
            help="Diagnostic verbosity: error (default, fail on errors), all (errors+warnings), none (silent)",
            short="e"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "args", kind=ArgKind.REMAINDER, help="Arguments passed to the script"
        ),

    ],
    examples=[
        ("jac run hello.jac", "Run a simple program"),
        ("jac run --no-cache app.jac", "Run without caching"),
        ("jac run --autonative app.jac", "Run with native auto-promotion"),
        ("jac run --profile prod app.jac", "Run with production profile"),
        ("jac run -e all app.jac", "Run and show all diagnostics (errors+warnings)"),
        ("jac run -e none app.jac", "Run silently, suppress all diagnostics"),
        ("jac run script.jac arg1 arg2", "Run with script arguments"),

    ],
    group="execution"
)
def run(
    filename: str,
    main: bool = True,
    cache: bool = True,
    autonative: bool = False,
    diagnostics: str = "",
    args: list = []
) -> int;

"""Run the specified entrypoint function in the given .jac file."""
@registry.command(
    name="enter",
    help="Run a specific entrypoint in a Jac program",
    args=[
        Arg.create("filename", kind=ArgKind.POSITIONAL, help="Path to .jac file"),
        Arg.create(
            "entrypoint", kind=ArgKind.POSITIONAL, help="Function/walker to invoke"
        ),
        Arg.create("args", kind=ArgKind.REMAINDER, help="Arguments for entrypoint"),
        Arg.create("main", typ=bool, default=True, help="Treat as __main__", short="m"),
        Arg.create("root", default="", help="Root executor ID", short="r"),
        Arg.create("node", default="", help="Starting node ID", short="n"),
        Arg.create(
            "profile",
            default="",
            short="",
            help="Configuration profile to load (e.g. prod, staging)"
        ),

    ],
    examples=[
        ("jac enter app.jac my_walker arg1 arg2", "Run walker with args"),
        ("jac enter --node data_node app.jac process", "Run with specific node"),

    ],
    group="execution"
)
def enter(
    filename: str,
    entrypoint: str,
    args: list = [],
    main: bool = True,
    `root: str = "",
    nd: str = ""
) -> int;

"""Start REST API server."""
@registry.command(
    name="start",
    help="Start REST API server for a Jac program",
    args=[
        Arg.create(
            "filename",
            kind=ArgKind.POSITIONAL,
            default="main.jac",
            help="Path to .jac file (default: main.jac)"
        ),
        Arg.create("port", typ=int, default=8000, help="Server port", short="p"),
        Arg.create("main", typ=bool, default=True, help="Treat as __main__", short="m"),
        Arg.create(
            "faux",
            typ=bool,
            default=False,
            help="Print docs only (no server)",
            short="f"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "dev",
            typ=bool,
            default=False,
            help="Enable HMR (Hot Module Replacement) mode",
            short="d"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "api_port",
            typ=int,
            default=0,
            help="Separate API port for HMR mode (0=same as port)"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "no_client",
            typ=bool,
            default=False,
            help="Skip client bundling/serving (API only)"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "profile",
            default="",
            short="",
            help="Configuration profile to load (e.g. prod, staging)"
        ),

    ],
    examples=[
        ("jac start", "Start server with default main.jac"),
        ("jac start app.jac", "Start server with specific file"),
        ("jac start --port 3000", "Start main.jac on port 3000"),
        ("jac start app.jac --faux", "Generate API docs without starting"),
        ("jac start --dev", "Start with hot module replacement"),
        ("jac start app.jac --dev --no-client", "HMR mode without client bundling"),
        ("jac start --profile prod", "Start with production profile"),

    ],
    group="execution"
)
def start(
    filename: str,
    port: int = 8000,
    main: bool = True,
    faux: bool = False,
    dev: bool = False,
    api_port: int = 0,
    no_client: bool = False
) -> int;

"""Debug a Jac program using Python debugger."""
@registry.command(
    name="debug",
    help="Debug a Jac program with Python debugger",
    args=[
        Arg.create("filename", kind=ArgKind.POSITIONAL, help="Path to .jac file"),
        Arg.create("main", typ=bool, default=True, help="Treat as __main__", short="m"),
        Arg.create(
            "cache", typ=bool, default=False, help="Use cached compilation", short="c"
        ),
        Arg.create(
            "profile",
            default="",
            short="",
            help="Configuration profile to load (e.g. prod, staging)"
        ),

    ],
    examples=[("jac debug myprogram.jac", "Debug a program"), ],
    group="execution"
)
def debug(filename: str, main: bool = True, cache: bool = False) -> int;
```

We want scoped-CSS support for client modules, the way a card.style.css sitting next to card.cl.jac should get its class names auto-scoped into one logical module. Build the subsystem that discovers a module's .style.css annex, hashes every class selector it declares with a per-module blake2s digest (truncated to eight hex chars, giving names like card-1a2b3c4d), and rewrites the stylesheet so each declared selector uses its hashed name while :global(...) selectors are unwrapped and left verbatim. Expose the resulting bare-to-hashed class map so the ECMAScript pass can rewrite matching className/class literals in the module. Include a ScopedStyleSheet type whose postinit parses the source CSS, a method to rewrite a JSX class value token by token, single-selector and full-stylesheet scoping routines that descend into grouping at-rules like @media and @supports but copy @keyframes and declaration blocks untouched, a loader returning the scoped sheet or None when no annex exists, and small helpers for skipping CSS strings and consuming brace-delimited blocks.

```jac
"""Scoped-style annex support for the `cl` (client) target.

A `.style.css` file that shares a base name with a `.cl.jac` module
(e.g. `card.style.css` alongside `card.cl.jac`) forms one logical module
with auto-scoped CSS classes. The compiler:

  1. Hashes every class selector declared in the annex with a per-module
     digest (`blake2s(module_path + class_name)`, truncated to 8 hex
     chars), producing names like `card-1a2b3c4d`.
  2. Rewrites the annex CSS so each declared selector uses the hashed
     form, leaving `:global(...)` selectors verbatim (the wrapper is
     stripped, the inner selector preserved).
  3. Exposes the hashed names so the ECMAScript pass can rewrite JSX
     `className`/`class` literals in the module that reference a declared
     class to the same hashed form.

The rewritten CSS is emitted as a sidecar artifact (`Module.gen.css`) and
a side-effect `import "./<base>.css";` is injected into the compiled JS so
the styles load with the component -- framework-neutral, no bundler config.

This subsystem is self-contained: annex discovery + CSS parse + selector
hashing all live here; the ECMAScript pass only consumes the resulting
`class_map` and `scoped_css`.
"""

import from hashlib { blake2s }
import from jaclang.jac0core.bccache { discover_style_annex }

"""A loaded, scoped `.style.css` annex for one client module.

    Construct via `load_style_annex`; `postinit` parses `source_css`,
    populating `class_map` (bare name -> hashed name) and `scoped_css`
    (the selector-rewritten stylesheet).
    """
obj ScopedStyleSheet {
    has module_path: str,
        css_path: str,
        source_css: str,
        class_map: dict[str, str] = {},
        scoped_css: str = '';

    def postinit -> None;
    """Rewrite a JSX `className`/`class` value, hashing each declared token.

        The value is split on whitespace; tokens that name a class declared
        in the annex are replaced with their hashed form, others are kept
        verbatim. Original inter-token spacing is collapsed to single
        spaces (semantically irrelevant for a class list).
        """
    def rewrite_class_value(value: str) -> str;
}

"""Hash a single class name with the module-scoped digest.

    Returns the scoped name `<class_name>-<8 hex>`. Deterministic for a
    given (module_path, class_name) pair, so the CSS selector rewrite and
    the JSX `className` rewrite agree.
    """
def hash_class_name(module_path: str, class_name: str) -> str;

"""Rewrite a CSS selector prelude, hashing declared class tokens.

    Class tokens (`.name`) are replaced with `.name-<hash>` and recorded in
    `class_map`; `:global(...)` regions are unwrapped and preserved
    verbatim; comments, strings, and attribute selectors are passed through
    untouched.
    """
def scope_selector(selector: str, module_path: str, class_map: dict[str, str]) -> str;

"""Rewrite a full stylesheet, scoping the class selectors of style rules.

    Walks rules with brace tracking: style-rule preludes are scoped via
    `scope_selector`; grouping at-rules (`@media`, `@supports`,
    `@container`, `@layer`, `@scope`) are descended into; other at-rules
    (`@keyframes`, `@font-face`, ...) and all declaration blocks are copied
    verbatim. Mutates `class_map` in place and returns the rewritten CSS.
    """
def scope_stylesheet(css: str, module_path: str, class_map: dict[str, str]) -> str;

"""Load and scope the `.style.css` annex for a module, or None if absent.

    `module_path` is the head module's source path (variant suffix is
    handled by `discover_style_annex`).
    """
def load_style_annex(module_path: str) -> (ScopedStyleSheet | None);

"""Advance past a CSS string literal. `i` is the opening quote; returns the
    index just after the matching close quote (backslash escapes honored)."""
def _skip_string(s: str, i: int) -> int;

"""Consume a brace-delimited block verbatim. `start` indexes the opening
    `{`; returns the block text (braces included) and the index after the
    matching `}`. Strings and comments inside are not brace-counted."""
def _consume_braced_block(css: str, start: int) -> tuple[(str, int)];

"""True if a rule prelude is a grouping at-rule whose block holds nested
    rules (`@media`, `@supports`, `@container`, `@layer`, `@scope`) rather
    than declarations."""
def _grouping_at_rule(prelude: str) -> bool;

glob __all__ = [
         'ScopedStyleSheet',
         'load_style_annex',
         'hash_class_name',
         'scope_selector',
         'scope_stylesheet'
     ];

```

Topology-index write hooks (no-ops when disabled). _is_enabled (env overrides toml), _get_root_anchor, _type_name, _get_type_mro, _index_edge_into / _unindex_edge_from, and the callbacks on_edge_created / on_edge_destroyed / on_node_saved / on_node_destroyed.

```jac
"""Topology index maintenance hooks.

These functions keep root topology indices in sync with graph mutations
(edge create/destroy, node save/destroy). All are no-ops when the
topology_index config flag is disabled.

Query planning lives in `jaclang.runtimelib.planner` — this module only
mutates the index in response to runtime events. The cleanup boundary is
explicit: anything that *reads* the index for a query goes through the
planner; anything that *writes* the index in response to a graph mutation
stays here.
"""

import from uuid { UUID }

"""Check if topology_index is enabled. The `JAC_TOPOLOGY_INDEX` env var
overrides the toml flag (truthy: 1 / true / yes / on)."""
def _is_enabled -> bool;

"""Get the root NodeAnchor that owns this anchor."""
def _get_root_anchor(anchor: any) -> any;

"""Get the archetype class name."""
def _type_name(`obj: object) -> str;

"""Get the user-defined MRO chain for a node/edge archetype, stopping at the
runtime base archetypes (Node/Edge/Walker/Archetype/object). Concrete type
appears at index 0."""
def _get_type_mro(`obj: object) -> list[str];

"""Record an edge in the given root's topology index. Used by
`on_edge_created` to mirror cross-root edges into the indexes of both
endpoint owners (otherwise reverse queries from the target side would
miss the edge entirely)."""
def _index_edge_into(root_anchor: any, source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Remove an edge from the given root's topology index. Mirror of
`_index_edge_into` used by `on_edge_destroyed`."""
def _unindex_edge_from(root_anchor: any, source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Called after an edge is created between source and target."""
def on_edge_created(source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Called when an edge is destroyed."""
def on_edge_destroyed(source: any, target: any, `edge: any) -> None;

"""Called when a node is saved/persisted. Ensures it's in the root's index."""
def on_node_saved(node_anchor: any) -> None;

"""Called when a node is destroyed."""
def on_node_destroyed(node_anchor: any) -> None;

```

Write the query planner that chooses an execution strategy for a graph QueryPlan across three layers — native backend pushdown, the root topology index, and bulk batch_get. Expose an execute_plan entry point that runs a QueryPlan against a memory (applying any post-filter and returning empty for trivial plans), an execute_path that runs an ObjectSpatialPath through the pushdown/mixed/floor ladder and returns NodeAnchors in edge order or None to signal fallback, and plan_chain / plan_chain_ordered helpers that resolve a hop chain on a root's topology index to a candidate UUID set.

```jac
"""Query planner — picks the execution strategy for a QueryPlan.

The planner is the only place that knows about all three layers:

  1. Backend native pushdown (`Memory.execute_plan`, declared via
     `Memory.capabilities()`). Fastest when the backend can handle the plan
     because it bypasses the topology_index entirely.
  2. Root topology_index (`TopologyIndex.resolve_chain[_ordered]`). The
     universal in-process narrowing path. Always available when the index is
     enabled and the relevant root carries one.
  3. `batch_get` (every backend has this). The bulk-load primitive used after
     narrowing to materialize anchors → archetypes.

Strategy selection:

  * `pushdown`  — `plan.needs() <= backend.capabilities()`. Hand the whole
                  plan to the backend; iterate its generator.
  * `mixed`     — topology_index resolves the chain to a candidate UUID set,
                  the planner attaches that set as `plan.id_in`, and the
                  reduced plan (now needing `id_in` + maybe `field_pushdown`)
                  goes to the backend if it covers those needs. Otherwise the
                  planner falls through to `floor`.
  * `floor`     — topology_index → `batch_get`. Pure in-process. Always
                  works as long as the index is populated.

The planner is also the one place that observes `JAC_QUERY_TRACE` to log
which strategy fired for which plan — invaluable when debugging unexpected
fallbacks or perf cliffs in CI.
"""

import os;
import logging;
import from collections.abc { Generator }
import from uuid { UUID }

import from jaclang.jac0core.archetype { Anchor, NodeAnchor }
import from jaclang.runtimelib.query_plan { QueryPlan }

glob logger = logging.getLogger(__name__),
     __all__ = ['execute_plan', 'execute_path', 'plan_chain', 'plan_chain_ordered'];


"""Top-level entry point: execute a QueryPlan against a memory.

Returns an iterable of NodeAnchor results. Applies `plan.post_filter` if set.
Trivial plans (no chain, no filters, no narrowing) return empty — callers
should use `Memory.query()` directly for unfiltered scans.

The signature deliberately accepts `any` for `mem` so the planner can be
called from the bootstrap-compiled runtime layer without a circular import on
the Memory type.
"""
def execute_plan(mem: any, plan: QueryPlan) -> list[any];


"""High-level entry point: execute an `ObjectSpatialPath` against a memory.

This is what the runtime's `refs()` calls. Builds the QueryPlan from the
path's destinations, walks the strategy ladder (pushdown / mixed / floor),
applies the final node filter post-narrowing, and returns the result as
NodeAnchors in canonical edge-walk order (single-hop) or arbitrary order
(multi-hop set narrowing).

Returns None to signal "no fast path applies" — the caller should fall back
to the legacy edge-walk via `edges_to_nodes`. This happens when:
  * the path has predicate filters the index can't express
  * the origin isn't persistent (no root → no topology_index)
  * the chain has no useful filter (full walk anyway)
  * topology_index is disabled and no backend pushdown applies
"""
def execute_path(
    mem: any, path: any, slc: (slice | None) = None
) -> (list[any] | None);


"""Resolve a chain on a given root's topology_index to a `set[UUID]`.

Used internally by `execute_path` (and available to callers that want the
candidate set without materializing anchors). Returns None when no fast
path applies (index disabled, root has no index, or origin not persistent)."""
def plan_chain(
    root_anchor: any,
    origin_ids: set[UUID],
    chain: list[tuple[(str | None), (str | None), int]]
) -> (set[UUID] | None);


"""Compatibility helper: resolve the final hop in canonical edge-insertion
order with `slc` applied. Returns None when no ordered fast path applies."""
def plan_chain_ordered(
    root_anchor: any,
    origin_ids: set[UUID],
    chain: list[tuple[(str | None), (str | None), int]],
    slc: slice
) -> (list[UUID] | None);

```

```jac
"""Shell completion script generation for bash, zsh, and fish."""

import from typing { cast }

"""Generate a static shell completion script from pre-processed command data."""
def static_shellcode(
    commands: list[dict[str, any]], executable: str = "jac", shell: str = "bash"
) -> str;

def _static_bash(commands: list[dict[str, any]], exe: str) -> str;

def _static_zsh(commands: list[dict[str, any]], exe: str) -> str;

def _static_fish(commands: list[dict[str, any]], exe: str) -> str;

glob _BASH_TEMPLATE = (
         '_%s_complete() {\n'
         '    local cur prev cmd\n'
         '    COMPREPLY=()\n'
         '    cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"\n'
         '    prev="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}"\n'
         '    cmd="${COMP_WORDS[1]}"\n'
         '\n'
         '    if [[ $COMP_CWORD -eq 1 ]]; then\n'
         '        COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "%s" -- "$cur"))\n'
         '        return\n'
         '    fi\n'
         '\n'
         '%s'
         '    case "$cmd" in\n'
         '%s\n'
         '    esac\n'
         '}\n'
         'complete -o default -o bashdefault'
         ' -F _%s_complete %s\n'
     ),
     _BASH_VALUE_BLOCK = (
         '    # Complete option values\n'
         '    case "$cmd" in\n'
         '%s\n'
         '    esac\n'
         '\n'
     ),
     _BASH_VALUE_CASE = (
         '        %s)\n'
         '            case "$prev" in\n'
         '%s\n'
         '            esac\n'
         '            ;;'
     ),
     _BASH_CMD_WITH_FILES = (
         '        %s)\n'
         '            case "$cur" in\n'
         '                -*) COMPREPLY=($(compgen'
         ' -W "%s" -- "$cur")) ;;\n'
         '            esac\n'
         '            ;;'
     ),
     _BASH_CMD_NO_FILES = (
         '        %s)\n'
         '            COMPREPLY=($(compgen'
         ' -W "%s" -- "$cur"))\n'
         '            ;;'
     ),
     _ZSH_TEMPLATE = (
         '#compdef %s\n'
         '_%s() {\n'
         '    local -a commands\n'
         '    commands=(\n'
         '%s\n'
         '    )\n'
         '\n'
         '    _arguments -C \\\n'
         '        \'1:command:->command\' \\\n'
         '        \'*::arg:->args\'\n'
         '\n'
         '    case $state in\n'
         '        command)\n'
         '            _describe \'command\' commands\n'
         '            ;;\n'
         '        args)\n'
         '            case $words[1] in\n'
         '%s\n'
         '            esac\n'
         '            ;;\n'
         '    esac\n'
         '}\n'
         '_%s "$@"\n'
     );

```

QueryPlan IR between the planner and storage backends. HopSpec(edge_type?, node_type?, direction=OUT); QueryPlan(root_id, chain of HopSpec, field_predicates dict with Mongo-style operators, id_in set, slc, node_type_final, post_filter) with is_trivial / needs / repr declarations. Document the backend capability strings and the execute_plan return contract.

```jac
"""QueryPlan IR — the contract between the runtime planner and storage backends.

A QueryPlan describes a graph query in storage-neutral terms so the planner can
either hand it to a backend's native `execute_plan` (e.g. MongoDB compound index
+ `_id $in` pushdown, Postgres jsonb GIN) or fall back to the universal floor
(root topology_index → set narrowing → `batch_get`).

The IR captures only the shapes we can actually optimize today; complex
predicate lambdas stay on the slow path. Anything not representable as a
declarative dict belongs in the post-filter the runtime applies above.

Capability strings backends declare via `Memory.capabilities()`:

  - `'type_pushdown'`   — backend can filter by archetype type natively
                          (e.g. an `arch_type` index in Mongo/Sqlite).
  - `'field_pushdown'`  — backend can apply declarative field predicates
                          on archetype data without loading rows
                          (e.g. Mongo `data.archetype.*` filter dict,
                          Postgres jsonb path ops).
  - `'id_in'`           — backend can filter by `_id IN (...)`; required
                          when the topology_index narrows to a candidate set
                          and we want the backend to materialize that subset.
  - `'slice'`           — backend can apply `(offset, limit)` natively
                          (otherwise the planner slices the result list).

A backend's `execute_plan(plan)` returns:
  - `Generator[Anchor, ...]`  when it fully handled the plan
  - `None`                    to opt out and let the planner use the floor

The planner trusts the backend's claim — if a plan needs `'field_pushdown'`
and the backend declares it, the result is taken as authoritative. Mixed
strategies (narrow with the index, materialize via backend `id_in`) are
composed by the planner, not by the backend.
"""

import from collections.abc { Callable }
import from uuid { UUID }
import from jaclang.jac0core.archetype { Anchor }

glob __all__ = ['HopSpec', 'QueryPlan'];


"""One hop in a path expression: `[edge_type? -[direction]-> node_type?]`.

`edge_type` / `node_type` are bare archetype class names (no module prefix);
the topology_index resolves them via MRO fan-out so subclass matches "just
work". `direction` mirrors `EdgeDir`: 1=IN, 2=OUT, 3=ANY.
"""
obj HopSpec {
    has edge_type: (str | None) = None,
        node_type: (str | None) = None,
        direction: int = 2;
}


"""Declarative query plan handed to backends or executed by the floor.

Fields are populated by `planner._build_plan_from_path` (the IR builder)
from the runtime's `ObjectSpatialPath`. None of these is required — a plan
with only `chain` and a `root_id` is the common case for `[root -->]`.

Field reference:

  - `root_id`         the root anchor that owns the subgraph. Used both as the
                      adjacency origin for the topology_index and as the
                      access-control scope for backends that partition by root.
  - `chain`           ordered list of HopSpec. Empty chain = "match anchors in
                      this root with no traversal" (e.g. for `query_by_type`-
                      style scans).
  - `field_predicates` archetype-field constraints, keyed by bare field name
                      with MongoDB-style operator values:
                          `{'age': {'$lt': 28}, 'status': 'active'}`
                      Backends prefix field names with whatever path they use
                      (`data.archetype.<f>` in Mongo, jsonb path in PG).
                      Operators understood across backends: `$eq`, `$ne`,
                      `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$in`, `$nin`. Anything
                      else is backend-specific.
  - `id_in`           when the planner has already narrowed to a candidate
                      set (typically via the topology_index), this carries
                      that set so the backend can do a single `_id IN (...)`
                      lookup. None means "no candidate narrowing applied".
  - `slc`             optional slice. The planner sets this when the user
                      wrote `[-->][0:50]` and the chain is pushdown-eligible.
                      Backends without `'slice'` capability should ignore it;
                      the planner slices afterwards.
  - `node_type_final` archetype class name to match on the final result set.
                      Distinct from chain hops because it can be checked
                      directly via the `arch_type` index without graph
                      traversal — the cheap path when chain is empty.
  - `post_filter`     opaque callable from the runtime; the planner applies
                      it AFTER any backend execution. Not pushdown-eligible.
"""
obj QueryPlan {
    has root_id: (UUID | None) = None,
        chain: list[HopSpec] = [],
        field_predicates: dict = {},
        id_in: (set[UUID] | None) = None,
        slc: (slice | None) = None,
        node_type_final: (str | None) = None,
        post_filter: (Callable[[Anchor], bool] | None) = None;

    def is_trivial -> bool;
    def needs -> set[str];
    def repr -> str;
}

```

I want a reusable icon component for the web build of my Jac app, wrapping Lucide (lucide-react). Set up a name-to-icon lookup for the glyphs I use — home, search, bell, user, heart, comment, repeat, edit, logout, lock, at-sign, a spark/star, calendar, close, send, image — and expose an Icon function taking a name plus size, color, stroke width, and a fill flag. When fill is on it should paint the glyph solid in its own color (for an active like or a brand mark); otherwise render it outlined. Keep the exact same <Icon name=.../> API that the native build uses so call sites don't change.

```jac
"""Icon set — WEB variant (Lucide via `lucide-react`, real DOM SVG).

The compiler picks `icon.native.cl.jac` (which uses `lucide-react-native`) for
the react-native target instead of this file, so the same `<Icon name=.../>`
call renders crisp Lucide vector icons on both platforms. `lucide-react` renders
plain `<svg>` and needs no `react-native-svg`, so the web bundle stays clean.
"""

cl {
    import from "lucide-react" {
        House,
        Search,
        Bell,
        User,
        Heart,
        MessageCircle,
        Repeat2,
        SquarePen,
        LogOut,
        Lock,
        AtSign,
        Star,
        Calendar,
        X,
        Send,
        Image as ImageIcon
    }

    # name → Lucide component. Same keys exist in icon.native.cl.jac.
    glob LUCIDE = {
             home: House,
             search: Search,
             bell: Bell,
             user: User,
             heart: Heart,
             comment: MessageCircle,
             repeat: Repeat2,
             edit: SquarePen,
             logout: LogOut,
             lock: Lock,
             at: AtSign,
             spark: Star,
             calendar: Calendar,
             close: X,
             send: Send,
             image: ImageIcon
         };

    """Render a Lucide icon by name. `fill` paints it solid in its own color
    (active like / brand mark); `width` is the stroke weight."""
    def:pub Icon(
        name: str, size: int, color: str, fill: bool, width: float
    ) -> JsxElement {
        Glyph = LUCIDE[name];
        return
            <Glyph
                size={size}
                color={color}
                fill={(color if fill else "none")}
                strokeWidth={width}
            />;
    }
}

```
